checks.evidence: “may, but is not required to, request supporting evidence” preserves discretion.
“If requested, the applicant must provide it within 8 business days of the request.”
“is not required to” makes requesting evidence optional rather than universal.

ratings.reason: Preserves the complete policy; the deadline's connection to the request is a supported clarification.

checks.evidence: “A reviewer may request supporting evidence” preserves permission.
“If requested, the applicant must provide it within 8 business days.”
“is not required to do so in every case.”

ratings.reason: Clearly preserves all source meaning without additions or material omissions.

cases.preference_reason: Both clearly preserve reviewer discretion and the conditional applicant deadline.

checks.evidence: “Release the shipment only after both the quality manager and the warehouse lead approve it” preserves the prerequisite.
“both the quality manager and the warehouse lead approve it in writing.”
“Verbal approvals do not count” excludes verbal approval from either named approver.

ratings.reason: Preserves both written approvals as necessary conditions and rejects verbal substitutes. No additional source meaning is omitted.

checks.evidence: “Release the shipment only after both the quality manager and the warehouse lead approve it” preserves the prerequisite.
“both the quality manager and the warehouse lead approve it in writing.”
“Verbal approval from either person does not count.”

ratings.reason: Preserves the complete release restriction, including the scope of the verbal-approval exclusion.

cases.preference_reason: Both communicate the same written-approval requirement clearly; the verbal-approval phrasing creates no meaningful difference.

checks.evidence: “either a valid badge or a temporary pass is presented” preserves the credential alternatives.
“only when a security officer is present” retains the additional condition.
“Both are not required” refers, in context, to the badge and pass.

ratings.reason: Preserves all access conditions. The final sentence is less idiomatic and less explicit about its referent, but the preceding credential alternatives resolve its meaning.

checks.evidence: “you present either a valid badge or a temporary pass” preserves either credential as sufficient for the credential condition.
“only when a security officer is present” preserves the officer-presence requirement.
“You do not need both.”

ratings.reason: Clearly preserves the alternative credentials and concurrent officer requirement. Direct address does not materially change the actor or scope.

cases.preference_reason: “You do not need both” expresses the credential rule more naturally and clearly than “Both are not required.”

checks.evidence: “Either party may terminate this agreement” preserves optional termination by either party.
“at least 45 calendar days’ written notice.”
“Termination does not affect the obligation to pay any fees already owed.”

ratings.reason: Preserves the termination permission, notice requirements, and continuing liability for existing fees.

checks.evidence: “Either party may terminate the agreement” preserves permission rather than obligation.
“at least 45 calendar days’ written notice.”
“Termination does not cancel fees already owed.”

ratings.reason: Preserves all source meaning in clear, compact wording.

cases.preference_reason: Both accurately and clearly express the same termination and payment rules.

checks.evidence: “Reimbursement covers actual, documented expenses” retains the qualifying expense category.
“up to GBP 175 per trip.”
“Claims must be submitted within 21 calendar days after the trip unless Finance grants a written exception” expresses the eligibility deadline as a submission requirement.
“unless Finance grants a written exception.”

ratings.reason: Preserves the expense limitation, per-trip cap, deadline, and written exception. In this reimbursement context, the submission requirement conveys the eligibility condition, though less explicitly than the source.

checks.evidence: “covers only actual, documented expenses” explicitly preserves the expense restriction.
“up to GBP 175 per trip.”
“Claims submitted more than 21 calendar days after the trip are ineligible” preserves the boundary and consequence.
“unless finance grants a written exception.”

ratings.reason: Explicitly preserves every restriction, deadline consequence, and exception without additional material claims.

cases.preference_reason: B states both the exclusive expense restriction and late-claim ineligibility explicitly, making the policy consequence clearer.
